positive: A verified Phase 2A.2 project projection can mint one sealed active-run binding that records the exact immutable pack path, pack fingerprint, projection fingerprint, source-resolution fingerprint, run identity, trust posture, and compatibility mode.
Resolving an active run validates the frozen binding and the complete bound pack inventory without consulting or being retargeted by current.json.
Changing current.json affects future selection only; an already-bound run continues to resolve the original valid content-addressed pack.
The official Requirements adapter resolves every governing rule from the validated frozen active-run pack and rejects relative rediscovery, current-working-directory lookup, and current.json lookup.
Bounded legacy schema-v1 continuation is read-only and explicitly classified; it cannot mint a new Full run binding or be silently promoted to schema v2.

Read-only status reports package, projection, selector, frozen-run, trust, compatibility, and provisioning-needed state without changing files, while explicit provision service behavior reuses the Phase 2A.2 transaction.

Focused proof covers immutable binding, selector changes after binding, altered or missing bound packs, incompatible fingerprints, safe legacy continuation, Requirements lookup through the frozen pack, read-only status, and explicit offline provision behavior.
negative: Phase 2B never contacts the network, executes pack content, mutates bundle bytes, rewrites an active-run binding, follows symlinks, trusts current.json for an active run, or silently upgrades legacy state.
Missing, altered, stale, incompatible, conflicting, or unsafe bound state fails closed with a categorical issue and leaves source, projection, selector, and run state unchanged.
A legacy schema-v1 pack can support only an already-authorized bounded continuation and can never authorize a new Full run.
This slice does not implement Full Start or Planning Lock wiring, MCP routing, host projection, new schemas, package registration, CLI dispatcher commands, or documentation.
